findings.message: When the commit's email and its login belong to different people, the new email-first branch always credits whoever holds the email. It does not check `c.verified` and never considers the conflict. `setGitHubIdentities` skips an email that someone else holds and tells the person to "ask an Admin". Until an Admin settles that, a person whose GitHub has verified the email can have their own GitHub-signed commits credited to the old holder. The old holder may be a row linked before 108 through a delivery link suggestion. Fix: when the email holder is not the identity matched by login, and that identity is a connected one, credit nobody (`userId: null`), so the conflict comes up for an Admin. Do not hand the commit to either person. Add that case to the table in ingest-112.test.ts.
findings.scenario: Before 108, Kasun's row holds a@lumen.test, verified through an accepted link suggestion. Later Nimal connects GitHub as @nimal-gh. GitHub has verified a@lumen.test on Nimal's account, but the connect skips it as "linked to another person". Nimal pushes a GitHub-signed commit (login nimal-gh, email a@lumen.test, verified=true). authorOf returns Kasun, so Kasun is drafted time for Nimal's work. Before this diff the commit was credited to Nimal.
